conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that the claim is supported by evidence, citing a landmark randomized clinical trial, WHO guidelines, and meta-analyses demonstrating that tenofovir started in the third trimester reduces mother-to-child transmission of HBV.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion:** The claim is **supported by evidence**; the view that it is false is not borne out by the retrieved sources.

**Evidence:**

1. **Randomized clinical trial (Pan et al., 2016, NEJM):** In a multicenter RCT, daily tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) during the third trimester reduced mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of HBV from 18% to 5% in mothers with high viral load. This is the landmark trial directly testing the claim.  
   https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa1508660

2. **WHO guideline recommendation:** WHO recommends tenofovir prophylaxis from the 28th week of pregnancy (third trimester) for HBsAg-positive pregnant women with HBV DNA ≥200,000 IU/mL, specifically to prevent MTCT. This reflects global expert consensus endorsing the practice.  
   https://www.aidsdatahub.org/sites/default/files/resource/who-pmtct-hepatitis-b-virus-2020.pdf

3. **Meta-analysis on efficacy and safety:** A meta-analysis found tenofovir effective and safe in preventing mother-to-infant HBV transmission, supporting its use in late pregnancy for highly viremic mothers.  
   https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30071845/

4. **Recent noninferiority trial (JAMA, 2024):** A trial compared starting tenofovir at gestational week 16 versus week 28; the week-28 arm served as the standard comparator, confirming that third-trimester initiation is an established, effective standard of care.  
   https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2826316

**Summary:** Multiple sources—an RCT, WHO guidelines, a meta-analysis, and a recent noninferiority trial—consistently support that tenofovir begun in the third trimester reduces MTCT in pregnant women with chronic HBV and high viral load. The evidence does not support the view that the claim is false.
